title: HuggingGPT: Solving AI Tasks with ChatGPT and its Friends in Hugging Face
summary: An LLM controller plans a user request into subtasks, picks a specialist model from Hugging Face for each subtask using model descriptions, runs them and summarizes the results. An early example of per-subtask model selection by an orchestrating LLM, though aimed at capability rather than cost.
key_idea: LLM planner assigns each decomposed subtask to a specialist model chosen by its description.
relevance_rationale: Background precedent for subtask-level model selection; no cost optimization.

title: SwiftSage: A Generative Agent with Fast and Slow Thinking for Complex Interactive Tasks
summary: A dual-process agent pairs a small fine-tuned encoder-decoder that proposes actions quickly with a large LLM that is invoked for planning and grounding when heuristics signal trouble. The combination beats ReAct, Reflexion and SayCan on 30 ScienceWorld tasks while calling the expensive LLM less often.
key_idea: Small imitation-learned policy acts by default; a large LLM is called only when heuristics detect difficulty.
relevance_rationale: Canonical big-little switching inside an agent loop; directly analogous to per-step downscaling.

title: A Dynamic LLM-Powered Agent Network for Task-Oriented Agent Collaboration
summary: DyLAN picks a team of agents for a task via an unsupervised Agent Importance Score computed on a preliminary trial, then lets the selected agents collaborate over a dynamic communication structure. It reports better results than fixed-team baselines at moderate compute and up to 25% accuracy gains on some MMLU subjects from team selection alone.
key_idea: Select which agents participate using contribution scores from a trial run.
relevance_rationale: Agent-selection and pruning precursor to AgentPrune/AgentDropout; cost is secondary.

title: Small LLMs Are Weak Tool Learners: A Multi-LLM Agent
summary: Alpha-UMi decomposes a tool-using agent into planner, caller and summarizer roles, each backed by its own small LLM, trained with a global-then-local progressive fine-tuning scheme. The modular multi-LLM agent outperforms a single fine-tuned LLM of the same backbone on tool-use benchmarks.
key_idea: Split one agent into role-specialized small LLMs (planner/caller/summarizer).
relevance_rationale: Role-level model assignment with small models; shows specialization can replace a single larger model.
found_via: web search: small LLMs weak tool learners

title: More Agents Is All You Need
summary: Shows that simply sampling many agent outputs and taking a majority vote (Agent Forest) scales LLM performance with the number of agents, and that the gain grows with task difficulty. Serves as a strong, cheap-to-build baseline against which elaborate multi-agent designs should be compared.
key_idea: Performance scales with the number of sampled agents under plain voting.
relevance_rationale: Baseline for when multi-agent structure is worth its cost.
found_via: web search: More agents is all you need

title: Language Agents as Optimizable Graphs
summary: GPTSwarm represents agents as computational graphs whose nodes query LLMs and whose edges carry information, and optimizes both node prompts and edge connectivity automatically. Edge optimization prunes or adds inter-agent links, making orchestration itself learnable.
key_idea: Treat multi-agent systems as optimizable graphs and learn which edges to keep.
relevance_rationale: Foundation for topology/pruning work (AgentPrune, G-Designer); not cost-driven itself.
found_via: arXiv title search: Language Agents as Optimizable Graphs

title: Rethinking the Bounds of LLM Reasoning: Are Multi-Agent Discussions the Key?
summary: Re-examines whether multi-agent discussion improves LLM reasoning and finds that a single agent with strong prompts (demonstrations) matches the best discussion frameworks across tasks and backbones. Multi-agent discussion only helps when no demonstrations are given.
key_idea: A well-prompted single agent matches multi-agent discussion.
relevance_rationale: Direct evidence on when multi-agent architecture is not worth its extra calls.

title: Mixture-of-Agents Enhances Large Language Model Capabilities
cost_reduction_reported: MoA-Lite reported as more cost-effective than GPT-4o with a 1.8% AlpacaEval 2.0 quality gain (per search summary of the paper)
summary: Layers of LLM agents each consume the previous layer's outputs and an aggregator synthesizes the final response; an all-open-source MoA reaches 65.1% on AlpacaEval 2.0 versus 57.5% for GPT-4 Omni. A lighter MoA-Lite configuration trades some quality for lower cost.
key_idea: Stack proposer LLMs in layers with an aggregator to exceed a single frontier model.
relevance_rationale: Heterogeneous multi-model composition; baseline for cost-aware MoA variants.

title: Scaling Large Language Model-based Multi-Agent Collaboration
summary: MacNet organizes up to a thousand agents on directed acyclic graphs and studies how performance changes as agent count grows, reporting a logistic collaborative scaling law and that irregular topologies beat regular ones. Provides evidence on the returns (and cost) of adding more agents.
key_idea: Collaborative scaling law: performance grows logistically with agent count.
relevance_rationale: Background on scaling agent count vs cost.

title: Improving Multi-Agent Debate with Sparse Communication Topology
cost_reduction_reported: Comparable or superior performance at significantly reduced computational cost; search summary cites over 40% input-token cost reduction in some configurations
summary: Studies communication connectivity in multi-agent debate and shows that sparse topologies match or beat fully connected debate at much lower compute. It also finds that giving stronger LLMs to more central agents helps, a form of role-aware model placement.
key_idea: Sparse debate graphs cut tokens; place stronger models at high-centrality nodes.
relevance_rationale: Both communication pruning and heterogeneous model placement by role.
found_via: web search: sparse communication topology debate

title: Agentless: Demystifying LLM-based Software Engineering Agents
cost_reduction_reported: $0.70 per issue at 32.00% on SWE-bench Lite, highest among open-source agents at the time
summary: Agentless replaces an autonomous coding agent with a fixed three-phase pipeline (localize, repair, validate) and reaches the best open-source SWE-bench Lite result at the time at about $0.70 per issue. It questions whether complex agent loops are needed for many software tasks.
key_idea: A fixed simple pipeline can beat complex agents on cost and accuracy.
relevance_rationale: Key architecture-level cost evidence: workflow vs agent.

title: AI Agents That Matter
cost_reduction_reported: Simple baselines match complex SOTA agents at far lower cost; the paper designs a joint cost-accuracy optimization that greatly reduces cost while maintaining accuracy (search summary cites 50x cost spread for similar accuracy)
summary: Critiques agent benchmarking: accuracy-only leaderboards produce needlessly costly agents, and simple baselines (retry, warming, escalation) sit on the cost-accuracy Pareto frontier. Also covers holdout sets, overfitting and reproducibility, and argues for jointly optimizing cost and accuracy.
key_idea: Evaluate agents on the cost-accuracy Pareto frontier, not accuracy alone.
relevance_rationale: Seed; foundational for cost-aware agent evaluation and simple escalation baselines.

title: Cut the Crap: An Economical Communication Pipeline for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
cost_reduction_reported: Comparable results to SOTA topologies at $5.6 vs $43.7; 28.1%-72.8% token reduction when plugged into existing MAS
summary: AgentPrune identifies communication redundancy in multi-agent pipelines and does one-shot pruning on the spatial-temporal message-passing graph to keep only useful messages. It reaches state-of-the-art-level accuracy at a fraction of token cost and improves robustness to adversarial agents.
key_idea: One-shot pruning of the inter-agent message graph removes redundant communication.
relevance_rationale: Seed; direct cost reduction inside MAS.

title: AgentSquare: Automatic LLM Agent Search in Modular Design Space
benchmarks: web, embodied, tool-use and game benchmarks (six)
summary: AgentSquare defines a modular agent design space (planning, reasoning, tool use, memory) and searches it through module evolution and recombination, using an in-context surrogate to skip weak designs. Found agents beat hand-crafted ones by 17.2% on average across six benchmarks.
key_idea: Search over modular agent designs with a surrogate performance predictor.
relevance_rationale: Agent architecture search; cost is not the main objective but the predictor reduces search cost.

title: Optima: Optimizing Effectiveness and Efficiency for LLM-Based Multi-Agent System
signals_used: reward: task score + token count + readability
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 2.8x performance gain with less than 10% of tokens vs vanilla MAS on information-heavy tasks
summary: Optima trains the agents of a multi-agent system with an iterative generate-rank-select-train loop (SFT, DPO and hybrids) whose reward balances task success, token efficiency and readability, using MCTS-style data generation. The trained MAS communicates far more tersely and outperforms both single-agent and vanilla MAS baselines.
key_idea: Train MAS agents with a reward that penalizes tokens to get efficient communication.
relevance_rationale: Seed; training-based MAS cost reduction.

title: G-Designer: Architecting Multi-agent Communication Topologies via Graph Neural Networks
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 95.33% token reduction on HumanEval
summary: G-Designer uses a variational graph auto-encoder over agent nodes and a task node to generate a task-adaptive communication topology for each task. It reaches strong accuracy while cutting token consumption on easy tasks and stays robust to adversarial agents.
key_idea: Generate a per-task communication topology with a graph auto-encoder.
relevance_rationale: Seed; query-adaptive topology reduces MAS cost.

title: AdaSwitch: Adaptive Switching between Small and Large Agents for Effective Cloud-Local Collaborative Learning
cost_reduction_reported: Competitive with cloud agent on some tasks while using much less computational overhead
summary: A small local agent handles simple reasoning steps and, when it introspectively detects an error, asks a larger cloud agent to take over that step. The step-level switching improves the local agent substantially and sometimes approaches the cloud agent at much lower cost.
key_idea: Local small agent escalates individual reasoning steps to a cloud LLM when it detects its own errors.
relevance_rationale: Step-level escalation inside a trajectory.

title: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Collaboration Networks for Software Development
summary: EvoMAC treats a multi-agent coding team like a network and updates agents and their links at test time via textual backpropagation from test-team feedback. It introduces rSDE-Bench for software-level requirements and outperforms prior multi-agent coders.
key_idea: Textual backpropagation to evolve a coding MAS at test time.
relevance_rationale: MAS self-evolution; cost not the focus.

title: EcoAct: Economic Agent Determines When to Register What Action
cost_reduction_reported: Over 50% reduction in computational cost on multi-step reasoning tasks while maintaining performance
summary: EcoAct gives the agent a single meta-tool to register tools on demand from their names, instead of loading all tool descriptions into context every step. Integrating tool registration into reasoning cuts cost by more than half on multi-step tasks without hurting accuracy.
key_idea: Register tools lazily inside the reasoning loop to shrink per-step context.
relevance_rationale: Seed; step-level tool-context cost lever.

title: SMoA: Improving Multi-agent Large Language Models with Sparse Mixture-of-Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Comparable to MoA with significantly lower computational cost
summary: Sparse Mixture-of-Agents adds response selection by a judge and early stopping so only a subset of agent outputs flows forward between layers, and gives agents distinct roles for diversity. It matches dense MoA at substantially lower compute.
key_idea: Sparsify MoA information flow with judge-based selection and early stopping.
relevance_rationale: Cost-aware MoA variant.

title: Magentic-One: A Generalist Multi-Agent System for Solving Complex Tasks
summary: Microsoft's Magentic-One uses an Orchestrator that plans, tracks progress and re-plans while directing specialist agents (web, file, coder, terminal). Its modular design allows different models per agent, and it reaches competitive results on GAIA, AssistantBench and WebArena.
key_idea: Orchestrator-plus-specialists architecture with swappable per-agent models.
relevance_rationale: Production-grade reference orchestration pattern supporting heterogeneous model assignment.

title: BudgetMLAgent: A Cost-Effective LLM Multi-Agent system for Automating Machine Learning Tasks
cost_reduction_reported: 94.2% cost reduction ($0.931 to $0.054 per run) with 32.95% vs 22.72% success rate compared to GPT-4 single agent on MLAgentBench
summary: BudgetMLAgent builds a multi-agent system around free or cheap base models, using profiling, retrieval of past observations, LLM cascades and occasional ask-the-expert calls to GPT-4 for planning. It beats a GPT-4 single agent on MLAgentBench at a small fraction of the cost.
key_idea: Cheap base model with cascades and rare expert calls for planning.
relevance_rationale: Concrete step-level escalation with large cost savings.
found_via: web search: single vs multi-agent cost

title: Rethinking Mixture-of-Agents: Is Mixing Different Large Language Models Beneficial?
summary: Finds that Self-MoA, which aggregates multiple samples from only the best single model, beats standard MoA that mixes different LLMs in many settings (+6.6% on AlpacaEval 2.0). Mixing models often lowers average quality; the paper characterizes when mixing helps.
key_idea: Mixing heterogeneous models is often worse than sampling the best one.
relevance_rationale: Caution on heterogeneous composition; informs model-mix decisions.

title: Multi-agent Architecture Search via Agentic Supernet
cost_reduction_reported: Requires only 6-45% of the inference cost of existing handcrafted or automated MAS while improving accuracy 0.54%-11.82%
summary: MaAS optimizes an agentic supernet, a distribution over multi-agent architectures, and samples a query-dependent architecture at inference so easy queries get light systems and hard ones get more operators. It cuts inference cost sharply versus handcrafted and automated MAS while improving accuracy and transferring across datasets and backbones.
key_idea: Sample a per-query multi-agent architecture from a learned supernet to allocate compute.
relevance_rationale: Seed; query-adaptive MAS cost allocation.

title: Talk Structurally, Act Hierarchically: A Collaborative Framework for LLM Multi-Agent Systems
summary: TalkHier introduces a structured communication protocol and hierarchical refinement for multi-agent LLM systems and reports gains over o1, AgentVerse and majority voting on QA and ad-text tasks. Relevant mainly as an orchestration pattern; cost is not reduced.
key_idea: Structured messages plus hierarchical evaluator teams.
relevance_rationale: Background orchestration pattern.

title: MasRouter: Learning to Route LLMs for Multi-Agent Systems
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 52.07% overhead reduction vs SOTA on HumanEval; 17.21%-28.17% overhead reduction when plugged into mainstream MAS; +1.8%-8.2% on MBPP
summary: Defines Multi-Agent System Routing: jointly choosing the collaboration mode, the agent roles and the LLM for each agent. A cascaded controller network builds the MAS step by step, improving accuracy and cutting cost versus prior MAS and routers, and can be plugged into existing frameworks.
key_idea: Cascaded controller jointly selects collaboration mode, roles and per-agent LLMs.
relevance_rationale: Seed; the core formulation of per-agent model routing in MAS.

title: Minions: Cost-efficient Collaboration Between On-device and Cloud Language Models
cost_reduction_reported: Naive Minion: 30.4x lower remote cost at 87% of frontier quality; MinionS: 5.7x lower cost at 97.9% of remote-only performance
benchmarks: financial, medical and scientific long-document reasoning tasks
summary: Studies local-remote collaboration where a small on-device model reads long documents and a frontier cloud model coordinates. In MinionS the remote model decomposes the task into chunk-level subtasks executed in parallel by the local model, cutting cloud cost 5.7x while keeping about 98% of quality. Together AI published a companion blog post on Minions.
key_idea: Frontier model decomposes; small local model executes many cheap subtasks.
relevance_rationale: Planner-big/executor-small division of labor with measured cost savings.

title: MAS-GPT: Training LLMs to Build LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
summary: MAS-GPT reframes MAS construction as generation: a fine-tuned mid-size LLM emits an executable query-specific MAS in one inference, trained on consistency-filtered query-MAS pairs. It outperforms 10+ MAS baselines while avoiding the repeated LLM calls of search-based MAS design.
key_idea: Generate an executable query-specific MAS in a single forward pass.
relevance_rationale: Query-adaptive MAS construction at low design-time cost.

title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
summary: Builds MAST, a taxonomy of 14 multi-agent failure modes in three categories (system design, inter-agent misalignment, task verification) from expert annotation of traces, plus an LLM-judge annotator and a 1600+ trace dataset. Shows that MAS gains on benchmarks are often minimal and that simple fixes give limited improvement.
key_idea: Taxonomy and dataset of why multi-agent systems fail.
relevance_rationale: Seed; evidence on when MAS is worth it and a failure-detection signal source.

title: AgentDropout: Dynamic Agent Elimination for Token-Efficient and High-Performance LLM-Based Multi-Agent Collaboration
cost_reduction_reported: 21.6% fewer prompt tokens and 18.4% fewer completion tokens with +1.14 performance vs SOTA
summary: AgentDropout learns which agents and edges to drop in each communication round by optimizing the graph adjacency matrices, removing redundant agents dynamically. It lowers token use and slightly improves accuracy over prior topology methods.
key_idea: Drop redundant agents and edges per round by optimizing communication graphs.
relevance_rationale: Seed; agent-level pruning for cost.

title: FlowReasoner: Reinforcing Query-Level Meta-Agents
summary: FlowReasoner is a reasoning meta-agent, distilled from DeepSeek-R1 and then trained with RL on execution feedback, that designs one multi-agent system per query. Its reward includes performance, complexity and efficiency terms, and it beats o1-mini by 10.52% across three code benchmarks.
key_idea: RL-trained meta-agent designs a per-query MAS with an efficiency term in the reward.
relevance_rationale: Query-level MAS design with cost-aware reward.

title: Towards Multi-Agent Reasoning Systems for Collaborative Expertise Delegation: An Exploratory Design Study
summary: An exploratory study of multi-agent reasoning design across expertise alignment, collaboration paradigm and scale. It finds domain-dependent benefits of expertise alignment, better results from diversity-driven integration than rigid decomposition, and diminishing returns versus computational cost as scale grows.
key_idea: Design-space study of when specialized multi-agent reasoning pays off.
relevance_rationale: Evidence on MAS design trade-offs and cost of scaling.

title: A Survey on Collaborative Mechanisms Between Large and Small Language Models
summary: Surveys collaboration between large and small language models, organizing mechanisms into pipeline, routing, auxiliary, distillation and fusion, with an edge-deployment emphasis. It lists open problems such as task allocation and system overhead.
key_idea: Taxonomy of LLM-SLM collaboration mechanisms.
relevance_rationale: Survey covering big-little collaboration.

title: MAS-ZERO: Designing Multi-Agent Systems with Zero Supervision
cost_reduction_reported: Accuracy gains up to 16.69% (reasoning), 16.66% (coding), 5.45% (agentic) while maintaining cost efficiency
summary: MAS-Zero is an inference-time meta-agent that designs, critiques and refines a MAS per problem without a validation set, and can collapse to a simpler system when that suffices. It beats manual and automatic MAS baselines while staying cost-efficient.
key_idea: Per-instance MAS design that can reduce to simpler systems when adequate.
relevance_rationale: Adaptive complexity per query, relevant to cost.

title: X-MAS: Towards Building Multi-Agent Systems with Heterogeneous LLMs
summary: X-MAS studies multi-agent systems where each agent function is powered by a different LLM, benchmarking 27 LLMs over 5 domains and 5 MAS functions (1.7M evaluations) to find the best model per domain-function pair. Switching to heterogeneous assignment improves MATH by up to 8.4% and AIME by 47% without changing structure.
key_idea: Pick the best LLM per agent function; heterogeneous MAS beats homogeneous.
relevance_rationale: Seed; empirical basis for role-level model assignment.

title: Single-agent or Multi-agent Systems? Why Not Both?
cost_reduction_reported: Hybrid cascading between MAS and single-agent improves accuracy 1.1-12% while reducing deployment cost up to 20%
summary: An empirical comparison of multi-agent and single-agent systems across agentic applications finds that MAS advantages shrink as frontier LLMs improve. Proposes request cascading between single-agent and multi-agent systems, gaining accuracy while cutting cost up to 20%.
key_idea: Cascade requests between single-agent and multi-agent systems.
relevance_rationale: Direct evidence and a mechanism for when MAS is worth it.
found_via: web search: single vs multi-agent cost

title: Multi-Agent Collaboration via Evolving Orchestration
cost_reduction_reported: Superior performance with reduced computational cost; token use falls during training
summary: A centralized orchestrator (puppeteer) is trained with REINFORCE to choose which agent acts next as the task state evolves, learning to skip unhelpful agents and terminate early. It improves performance while lowering compute, converging to compact cyclic structures.
key_idea: RL orchestrator sequences agents step by step and prunes low-utility ones.
relevance_rationale: Step-level agent selection with cost-aware RL.

title: RMoA: Optimizing Mixture-of-Agents through Diversity Maximization and Residual Compensation
cost_reduction_reported: Significantly reduces computational overhead vs MoA
benchmarks: alignment, math reasoning, code generation, multitask understanding
summary: Residual MoA selects diverse responses via embedding similarity, adds residual extraction/aggregation agents to preserve cross-layer information, and stops adaptively when residuals converge. It gets state-of-the-art MoA results with less compute.
key_idea: Diversity-based response selection and adaptive termination in MoA.
relevance_rationale: Cost-aware MoA variant.

title: Small Language Models are the Future of Agentic AI
summary: NVIDIA's position paper argues that small language models are capable enough, better suited and far cheaper for most repetitive, narrow invocations inside agentic systems, and that heterogeneous agents mixing SLMs and LLMs are the natural design. Outlines an LLM-to-SLM conversion algorithm from agent usage logs.
key_idea: Most agent calls should go to SLMs; convert LLM agents to SLMs using logged usage.
relevance_rationale: Seed; central thesis for subagent downscaling with a log-driven conversion recipe.

title: Adaptive Graph Pruning for Multi-Agent Communication
cost_reduction_reported: Over 90% decrease in token consumption with 2.58%-9.84% performance increase
benchmarks: six benchmarks: general reasoning, math reasoning, code generation
summary: Adaptive Graph Pruning jointly learns how many agents to use (hard pruning) and which edges to keep (soft pruning) per task through a two-stage training strategy. It improves accuracy and cuts tokens by over 90% with only a few training steps.
key_idea: Jointly prune agent count and communication edges per task.
relevance_rationale: MAS pruning for cost.

title: MasHost Builds It All: Autonomous Multi-Agent System Directed by Reinforcement Learning
summary: MasHost builds query-adaptive multi-agent graphs with RL, sampling roles and interactions jointly and optimizing accuracy, efficiency and component rationality via a Hierarchical Relative Policy Optimization method. It beats competitive MAS construction baselines on six benchmarks.
key_idea: RL-driven autonomous MAS graph construction with efficiency objective.
relevance_rationale: Query-adaptive MAS design with efficiency term.

title: Router-R1: Teaching LLMs Multi-Round Routing and Aggregation via Reinforcement Learning
cost_reduction_reported: Superior performance with cost management across 7 QA benchmarks (no single headline ratio in abstract)
benchmarks: seven general and multi-hop QA benchmarks
summary: Router-R1 makes the router an LLM that interleaves thinking and routing actions over multiple rounds, calling different LLMs and folding their answers into its context. It is trained with RL using format, outcome and cost rewards and generalizes to unseen models through simple descriptors.
key_idea: An RL-trained LLM router that calls models over multiple rounds with a cost reward.
relevance_rationale: Multi-round (trajectory-level) routing with cost-aware RL.

title: Efficient LLM Collaboration via Planning
cost_reduction_reported: Comparable performance to large proprietary models with drastically reduced inference API cost
summary: COPE lets small and large models alternate as planner and executor in a multi-stage cascade, with plans acting as a lightweight intermediate that guides the executor. It reaches large-model performance on math, code, open-ended and agent tasks at much lower API cost.
key_idea: Plans as a cheap intermediate in a small/large planner-executor cascade.
relevance_rationale: Planner-executor model split with escalation.

title: Assemble Your Crew: Automatic Multi-agent Communication Topology Design via Autoregressive Graph Generation
cost_reduction_reported: Significantly greater token efficiency than prior topology designers
summary: ARG-Designer generates a MAS collaboration graph from scratch autoregressively, deciding the number of agents, their roles and links conditioned on the task query. It beats template-modification methods and uses fewer tokens.
key_idea: Autoregressive generation of agent set and topology per query.
relevance_rationale: Query-adaptive MAS composition for efficiency.

title: MAO-ARAG: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation
cost_reduction_reported: Maintains cost and latency within acceptable limits while achieving high answer quality
summary: MAO-ARAG uses an RL-trained planner agent that assembles a per-query RAG workflow from executor agents (reformulation, selection, generation), rewarded on F1 minus a cost penalty. It adapts pipeline complexity to query difficulty.
key_idea: RL planner assembles per-query agent workflows with a cost penalty.
relevance_rationale: Cost-penalized per-query agent orchestration.

title: Efficient Agents: Building Effective Agents While Reducing Cost
cost_reduction_reported: Retains 96.7% of OWL's performance while reducing cost from $0.398 to $0.228 per task (28.4% better cost-of-pass) on GAIA
summary: OPPO's systematic study of the efficiency-effectiveness trade-off in agents on GAIA, varying LLM backbone, framework modules and test-time scaling and scoring them with cost-of-pass. The findings yield Efficient Agents, a framework sized to task needs that keeps most of OWL's accuracy at much lower cost.
key_idea: Measure each agent design choice with cost-of-pass and drop components with diminishing returns.
relevance_rationale: Seed; directly about architecture-level cost reduction including backbone choice.

title: RCR-Router: Efficient Role-Aware Context Routing for Multi-Agent LLM Systems with Structured Memory
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 30% token reduction while improving or maintaining answer quality
summary: RCR-Router routes only the relevant subset of shared memory to each agent based on its role and task stage under a strict token budget, and iteratively merges outputs back into structured memory. It cuts tokens while keeping answer quality on multi-hop QA.
key_idea: Role- and stage-aware context routing to each agent under a token budget.
relevance_rationale: Context-level cost lever for MAS.
found_via: arXiv title search: routing multi-agent system LLM

title: SafeSieve: From Heuristics to Experience in Progressive Pruning for LLM-based Multi-Agent Communication
cost_reduction_reported: 94.01% average accuracy with 12.4%-27.8% token reduction; 13.3% deployment cost reduction in heterogeneous settings
summary: SafeSieve progressively prunes inter-agent communication, starting from LLM-based semantic scoring and moving to experience-driven refinement, while clustering to keep coherent agent groups. It reduces tokens and cost, including in heterogeneous-model deployments, and is robust to prompt injection.
key_idea: Progressive heuristic-to-experience pruning of MAS communication.
relevance_rationale: MAS pruning with heterogeneous-deployment cost results.

title: Dynamic Speculative Agent Planning
cost_reduction_reported: Comparable efficiency to fastest lossless acceleration while reducing total cost by 30% and unnecessary cost by up to 60%
summary: Dynamic Speculative Planning uses a cheaper model to draft agent plans speculatively and an online, asynchronous RL policy to decide how far to speculate, with a single knob trading latency against dollar cost. It keeps outputs lossless while cutting cost relative to prior speculative agents.
key_idea: Online RL tunes speculative planning with a cheap drafter to balance latency and cost.
relevance_rationale: Big-little model use within agent planning, learned online.

title: Towards Generalized Routing: Model and Agent Orchestration for Adaptive and Efficient Inference
cost_reduction_reported: Superior cost-efficiency and scalability vs existing routers (no single number in abstract)
summary: MoMA routes each query either to an LLM or to a specialized agent, using profiled model capabilities for LLM routing and a context-aware state machine with dynamic masking for agent selection. It targets mixed ecosystems of models and domain agents.
key_idea: Unified router over both LLMs and agents.
relevance_rationale: Routing among agents as well as models.
found_via: arXiv title search: model routing agentic

title: Difficulty-Aware Agentic Orchestration for Query-Specific Multi-Agent Workflows
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 11.21% higher accuracy with up to 36% lower cost (per search summary of the paper); abstract reports gains in accuracy and efficiency on six benchmarks
summary: DAAO predicts query difficulty with a VAE, allocates workflow depth and operators accordingly, and routes each operator to an LLM with a cost- and performance-aware router, updating difficulty estimates from workflow outcomes. Simple queries get lighter workflows and cheaper models.
key_idea: Difficulty-driven workflow depth plus per-operator LLM routing.
relevance_rationale: Per-node model routing within query-specific workflows.

title: Reducing Cost of LLM Agents with Trajectory Reduction
cost_reduction_reported: Input tokens reduced 39.9%-59.7% and total cost 21.1%-35.9% with the same agent performance
summary: AgentDiet removes useless, redundant and expired information from coding-agent trajectories at inference time, using a cheaper reflection model over a sliding window. It cuts input tokens and total cost substantially with no loss in resolve rate.
key_idea: Prune waste from growing agent trajectories during execution.
relevance_rationale: Context-level cost lever for long-horizon agents; uses a cheaper model for the reduction step.

title: MAS$^2$: Self-Generative, Self-Configuring, Self-Rectifying Multi-Agent Systems
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 19.6% gains over SOTA MAS while staying on the cost-performance Pareto frontier
summary: MAS^2 uses a generator-implementer-rectifier meta-agent team, trained with Collaborative Tree Optimization, to compose and adaptively fix a target multi-agent system per task. It improves on prior automatic MAS and generalizes to unseen backbones without excessive token cost.
key_idea: A MAS that builds and rectifies other MAS at run time.
relevance_rationale: Automatic MAS construction on the cost-performance frontier.

title: AutoMaAS: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Architecture Search for Large Language Models
cost_reduction_reported: 1.0-7.1% performance improvement with 3-5% lower inference cost vs SOTA
summary: AutoMaAS extends agentic supernet search with automatic operator generation, fusion and elimination based on performance-cost analysis, plus online feedback for continual refinement. Gains over MaAS are modest in both accuracy and cost.
key_idea: Self-evolving supernet with cost-aware operator lifecycle.
relevance_rationale: Follow-up to MaAS with cost-aware search.

title: Small Language Models for Agentic Systems: A Survey of Architectures, Capabilities, and Deployment Trade offs
cost_reduction_reported: Reports SLMs can match LLMs on tool use/function calling at 10x-100x lower token cost with guided decoding (synthesized evidence)
summary: Surveys evidence that 1-12B models suffice for schema-constrained agent work and formalizes SLM-default, LLM-fallback designs with uncertainty-aware routing and verifier cascades. Proposes production metrics such as cost per successful task and schema validity rate.
key_idea: Default to SLMs, fall back to LLMs via uncertainty and verifiers.
relevance_rationale: Practical blueprint for step-level SLM-first agents.
found_via: OpenAlex search: LLM agent cascade small large

title: Speculative Actions: A Lossless Framework for Faster Agentic Systems
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 55% next-action prediction accuracy, up to 20% latency reduction
summary: Speculative Actions uses fast models to guess an agent's next actions and executes them in parallel, committing only when the main model agrees, analogous to speculative decoding. It gives lossless latency savings and analyzes the cost-latency trade-off of speculative breadth.
key_idea: Speculate agent actions with a small model; verify with the large one.
relevance_rationale: Big-little pairing within agent loops, latency-focused.

title: AgentRouter: A Knowledge-Graph-Guided LLM Router for Collaborative Multi-Agent Question Answering
summary: Formulates multi-agent QA as routing over agents with a heterogeneous GNN on a graph linking queries, entities and agents, trained with soft supervision from empirical agent performance, then aggregates weighted agent outputs. Beats single-agent and ensemble baselines.
key_idea: GNN-based routing among agents from a query knowledge graph.
relevance_rationale: Routing among agents; not primarily cost-driven.

title: Dynamic Generation of Multi-LLM Agents Communication Topologies with Graph Diffusion Models
cost_reduction_reported: Generates sparse, efficient topologies that significantly outperform prior methods (no single number in abstract)
summary: Guided Topology Diffusion builds multi-agent communication graphs iteratively with a discrete graph diffusion model steered by a lightweight proxy that predicts accuracy, utility and cost. The result is sparse task-adaptive topologies that save tokens.
key_idea: Diffusion-generated MAS topologies guided by a cost-aware proxy.
relevance_rationale: Cost-aware topology generation.

title: Holistic Agent Leaderboard: The Missing Infrastructure for AI Agent Evaluation
venue_or_source: arXiv (reported as ICLR 2026 in secondary sources)
cost_reduction_reported: Pareto frontiers of accuracy vs cost; e.g., higher reasoning effort reduced accuracy in most runs
benchmarks: 9 benchmarks in coding, web navigation, science, customer service
summary: HAL provides a standardized harness that runs agent evaluations in parallel on hundreds of VMs, and reports 21,730 rollouts over 9 models and 9 benchmarks (about $40,000) with cost-accuracy Pareto analysis. LLM-aided log inspection surfaces behaviors like searching for benchmark answers; all 2.5B tokens of logs are released.
key_idea: Standardized, cost-aware agent leaderboard with released logs.
relevance_rationale: Seed; key evaluation infrastructure and cost-accuracy evidence across scaffolds and models.

title: Verification-Aware Planning for Multi-Agent Systems
summary: VeriMAP's planner decomposes tasks, models dependencies and writes verification functions for each subtask, so executors can be checked and retried. Because executors get well-scoped subtasks, cheaper models can execute them, partly offsetting planner cost.
key_idea: Planner writes per-subtask verifiers so executors can be smaller.
relevance_rationale: Planner-executor split enabling cheaper executors with verification.

title: Stop Wasting Your Tokens: Towards Efficient Runtime Multi-Agent Systems
cost_reduction_reported: Reduces Smolagents token consumption by 29.68% on GAIA without lowering success rate
summary: SupervisorAgent is a lightweight runtime supervisor triggered by an LLM-free filter that intervenes at critical points to correct errors, curb inefficient behavior and clean observations, without changing the base agent. It cuts token usage by about 30% on GAIA at equal success.
key_idea: Runtime supervision triggered cheaply to stop wasteful agent behavior.
relevance_rationale: Architecture-level MAS token reduction.

title: Controlling Performance and Budget of a Centralized Multi-agent LLM System with Reinforcement Learning
cost_reduction_reported: Single system surpasses best expert LLM under high budget while staying strong in low-budget modes
summary: CoRL trains a controller LLM with RL to selectively call a pool of expert LLMs, maximizing performance while minimizing cost, and conditions on a budget so one system can operate at multiple cost levels. It beats the best single expert at high budget.
key_idea: Budget-conditioned RL controller that decides which expert LLMs to invoke.
relevance_rationale: Controllable cost in centralized multi-LLM agents.

title: MALBO: Optimizing LLM-Based Multi-Agent Teams via Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization
cost_reduction_reported: Over 45% lower average configuration cost vs random search at comparable performance; heterogeneous teams up to 65.8% cheaper than homogeneous at max performance
summary: MALBO frames assigning LLMs to agent roles as multi-objective Bayesian optimization over accuracy and cost, using GP surrogates over a continuous LLM feature space and expected hypervolume improvement. It finds heterogeneous teams that are much cheaper than homogeneous ones.
key_idea: Multi-objective BO over per-role LLM assignments.
relevance_rationale: Directly optimizes role-level model assignment for cost.

title: ReflexGrad: Within-Episode Failure Recovery in LLM Agents via Progress-Gated Dual-Process Routing
summary: ReflexGrad routes within an episode between a fast refinement process and a slow causal-diagnosis process when consecutive low progress scores trigger a gate. It raises Qwen-3-8B from 35.1% to 75.4% on ALFWorld and beats compute-matched LATS and ToT.
key_idea: Progress-gated switching between fast and slow processes inside a trajectory.
relevance_rationale: Progress signal as a trigger for heavier processing within trajectories.

title: Budget-Aware Tool Use Enables Effective Agent Scaling
cost_reduction_reported: Budget-aware methods push the cost-performance Pareto frontier under a unified token+tool cost metric
summary: Shows that simply raising tool-call budgets does not help web agents because they lack budget awareness, and introduces a Budget Tracker plug-in and BATS, which adapts planning and verification to the remaining budget. Proposes a unified cost metric over tokens and tool calls.
key_idea: Make agents budget-aware to scale tool use efficiently.
relevance_rationale: Tool-call cost control within agents.

title: Aragog: Just-in-Time Model Routing for Scalable Serving of Agentic Workflows
cost_reduction_reported: 50.0-217.0% higher max serving throughput and 32.5-78.9% lower median latency at peak rates with accuracy comparable to the most expensive configurations
summary: Aragog assigns workflow agents to LLMs progressively during execution: a one-time routing step finds all accuracy-preserving configurations, and a cheap per-stage scheduler picks among them based on current system load. It greatly improves serving throughput and latency.
key_idea: Just-in-time per-stage model reassignment driven by live load.
relevance_rationale: Per-stage model assignment in agent workflows with systems evidence.
found_via: arXiv title search: model routing agentic

title: Reason-Plan-ReAct: A Reasoner-Planner Supervising a ReAct Executor for Complex Enterprise Tasks
summary: RP-ReAct splits an enterprise agent into a reasoner-planner (a large reasoning model) that plans and reviews each sub-step and proxy-execution agents that carry out tool calls ReAct-style, with external storage for large tool outputs. It improves reliability over single-agent baselines on ToolQA.
key_idea: Reasoning-model planner supervising ReAct executors.
relevance_rationale: Planner-executor role split for enterprise tasks.

title: Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems
cost_reduction_reported: Relative change vs single agent ranges from +80.8% (decomposable financial reasoning) to -70.0% (sequential planning)
summary: Google Research runs 260 controlled configurations across five architectures (single-agent and four multi-agent types) and six benchmarks, fitting a predictive model of when coordination helps. Multi-agent gains saturate as single-agent capability rises, tool-heavy tasks incur multi-agent overhead, and mismatched coordination hurts performance. A companion Google Research blog post ('Towards a science of scaling agent systems: When and why agent systems work') summarizes the findings.
key_idea: Predictive scaling principles for when multi-agent architectures help.
relevance_rationale: Core evidence for when multi-agent is worth it.

title: AgentBalance: Backbone-then-Topology Design for Cost-Effective Multi-Agent Systems under Budget Constraints
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 10% and 22% performance gains under matched token-cost and latency budgets
summary: AgentBalance first matches heterogeneous LLM backbones to roles under explicit token-cost and latency budgets, then generates a latency-aware communication topology. It outperforms topology-first methods at equal budgets and works as a plug-in for existing MAS.
key_idea: Backbone-then-topology MAS design under explicit budgets.
relevance_rationale: Role-level model assignment under deployment budgets.

title: Small Language Models for Efficient Agentic Tool Calling: Outperforming Large Models with Targeted Fine-tuning
summary: AWS authors fine-tune a 350M-parameter OPT model for one epoch on tool-calling data and report a 77.55% ToolBench pass rate, above ChatGPT-CoT and ToolLLaMA baselines. Argues targeted SLMs can replace LLMs in routine enterprise agent steps.
key_idea: A tiny fine-tuned SLM can handle tool-calling steps.
relevance_rationale: Evidence for downscaling tool-call steps.

title: Efficient Mixture-of-Agents Serving via Tree-Structured Routing, Adaptive Pruning, and Dependency-Aware Prefill-Decode Overlap
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 90% lower end-to-end latency with accuracy within +/-1% of dense MoA
summary: Co-designs MoA serving with a tree topology for sparse communication, runtime skipping of downstream agents based on agreement and confidence, and overlapping prefill with decode across dependent agents. Latency drops sharply at near-equal accuracy.
key_idea: Sparse tree MoA with confidence-based agent skipping and pipelined serving.
relevance_rationale: Serving-level MoA efficiency.

title: HybridFlow: Resource-Adaptive Subtask Routing for Efficient Edge-Cloud LLM Inference
cost_reduction_reported: Reduces latency and cloud API usage while maintaining competitive accuracy (no single number in abstract)
summary: HybridFlow decomposes a query into a subtask DAG, runs unlocked subtasks in parallel and routes each subtask online to an edge SLM or cloud LLM via a learned benefit-cost utility and a budget-aware rule. It improves the cost-accuracy trade-off over per-query routing.
key_idea: Subtask-level edge/cloud routing with a learned utility under budgets.
relevance_rationale: Subtask-level model routing with budgets.

title: Bayesian Orchestration of Multi-LLM Agents for Cost-Aware Sequential Decision-Making
cost_reduction_reported: Total cost reduced by $294,000 (34%) vs best single-LLM baseline on 1000-resume screening simulation
summary: Treats several LLMs as likelihood models and combines them with Bayes rule for sequential decisions under asymmetric error costs, choosing actions by expected cost and gathering information by value of information. In a resume-screening simulation it lowers total decision cost by 34%.
key_idea: Bayesian aggregation of multiple LLMs for cost-aware sequential decisions.
relevance_rationale: Decision cost rather than inference cost; tangentially relevant orchestration.

title: EvoRoute: Experience-Driven Self-Routing LLM Agent Systems
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 80% lower execution cost and over 70% lower latency while sustaining or improving performance on GAIA and BrowseComp+
summary: EvoRoute frames the Agent System Trilemma of performance, cost and latency and selects a Pareto-optimal LLM backbone at every step using a growing knowledge base of past experience, refining its policy from environment feedback. Plugged into off-the-shelf agent systems it cuts cost by up to 80%.
key_idea: Experience-driven per-step backbone selection that self-evolves.
relevance_rationale: Per-step model routing inside agents with large reported savings.

title: When Single-Agent with Skills Replace Multi-Agent Systems and When They Fail
cost_reduction_reported: Substantially reduced token usage and latency while maintaining competitive accuracy (preliminary)
summary: Argues a multi-agent system can be compiled into a single agent that selects from a skill library, trading communication for skill selection, and finds preliminary token and latency savings. Skill-selection accuracy shows a sharp phase transition as the library grows, which hierarchical routing mitigates.
key_idea: Compile MAS into a single agent with skills; watch the skill-library capacity limit.
relevance_rationale: Architecture-level alternative to MAS with cost savings.

title: Orchestrating Intelligence: Confidence-Aware Routing for Efficient Multi-Agent Collaboration across Multi-Scale Models
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 12.88% higher accuracy and up to 79.78% lower cost vs baseline MAS
summary: OI-MAS routes, at each reasoning stage, to an agent role and a model scale from a heterogeneous pool of multi-scale LLMs, using a confidence-aware mechanism to avoid unnecessary use of large models. It raises accuracy and cuts cost versus uniform-model MAS.
key_idea: State-dependent routing of roles and model sizes with confidence gating.
relevance_rationale: Direct step/role-level model-scale routing in MAS.
found_via: arXiv title search: model routing agentic

title: ACE-Router: Generalizing History-Aware Routing from MCP Tools to the Agent Web
summary: ACE-Router trains history-aware routers on synthesized multi-turn trajectories over a tool/agent dependency graph to select among very large MCP tool and agent pools. It generalizes to agent selection in multi-agent settings and scales to massive candidate spaces.
key_idea: History-aware router for tools and agents in large ecosystems.
relevance_rationale: Tool/agent routing inside trajectories.

title: SC-MAS: Constructing Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent Systems with Edge-Level Heterogeneous Collaboration
cost_reduction_reported: +3.35% accuracy with 15.38% lower cost on MMLU; +3.53% accuracy with 12.13% lower cost on MBPP
summary: SC-MAS models a MAS as a directed graph with edge-level collaboration strategies and uses a controller to pick roles, per-edge strategies and a backbone LLM for each agent per query. It improves accuracy while reducing cost relative to MasRouter-style homogeneous-mode routing.
key_idea: Jointly route roles, per-edge collaboration styles and per-agent LLMs.
relevance_rationale: Extends MasRouter with heterogeneous collaboration and backbone allocation.

title: Adaptive Orchestration: Scalable Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems
cost_reduction_reported: Maintains high task success while minimizing token consumption vs static agent swarms (no number in abstract)
summary: Proposes a self-evolving concierge that hires specialized sub-agents on demand based on live conversation analysis, evicts them with an LRU policy, and prunes history. Aims to avoid both monolithic context pollution and static swarm overhead.
key_idea: Hire and evict sub-agents dynamically instead of running a static swarm.
relevance_rationale: Architecture idea with limited evaluation detail.

title: Do We Always Need Query-Level Workflows? Rethinking Agentic Workflow Generation for Multi-Agent Systems
cost_reduction_reported: Average 0.61% degradation while cutting token usage by up to 83%
summary: Shows that a small set of top task-level workflows covers as many queries as per-query workflow generation, and that exhaustive execution-based evaluation is costly and unreliable. SCALE replaces full validation runs with calibrated self-prediction, cutting optimization tokens up to 83%.
key_idea: Per-query workflow generation is often unnecessary; evaluate cheaply.
relevance_rationale: Questions the cost of query-level MAS design.

title: Can Small Agents Collaborate to Beat a Single Large Language Model?
summary: Controlled comparisons show a minimal MAS of small models (one orchestrator plus specialist sub-agents) can beat much larger single-agent models on tool-heavy tasks. Reasoning at the orchestrator gives the biggest gains, while sub-agent reasoning adds little; orchestrator capacity drives performance.
key_idea: Spend capacity on the orchestrator; sub-agents can be small.
relevance_rationale: Direct evidence on where to allocate model capacity across roles.

title: RouteMoA: Dynamic Routing without Pre-Inference Boosts Efficient Mixture-of-Agents
cost_reduction_reported: 89.8% cost reduction and 63.6% latency reduction in large-scale model pool vs MoA
summary: RouteMoA screens candidate models with a lightweight scorer before any inference, refines scores with judges using existing outputs, and ranks models by performance, cost and latency. It outperforms MoA while cutting cost by about 90% in large pools.
key_idea: Pre-inference routing to pick which models join each MoA layer.
relevance_rationale: Router-driven sparsification of multi-model ensembles.

title: EffGen: Enabling Small Language Models as Capable Autonomous Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Prompt compression of 70-80% (57% average); outperforms LangChain, AutoGen and Smolagents on 13 benchmarks
summary: EffGen is an open-source agent framework tuned for small models, combining prompt compression for tool calling, dependency-aware task decomposition, complexity-based routing and a unified memory system. Prompt optimization helps small models more while routing helps larger ones more.
key_idea: Agent framework engineered for SLMs with complexity routing.
relevance_rationale: Practical SLM-first agent stack.

title: Symphony-Coord: Adaptive Routing for Multi-Agent LLM Systems
summary: Symphony-Coord casts agent selection for subtasks as an online contextual bandit, with a candidate-screening step and a LinUCB selector updated by delayed post-execution feedback, and proves sublinear regret. It improves routing efficiency and recovery under shifts and agent failures.
key_idea: Contextual-bandit routing of subtasks to agents.
relevance_rationale: Online learning for agent routing.

title: Towards a Science of Collective AI: LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems Need a Transition from Blind Trial-and-Error to Rigorous Science
summary: A position paper arguing MAS research needs a collaboration gain metric that separates true collaboration benefits from simply spending more budget, plus a factor library for attribution. Relevant to judging whether multi-agent designs beat equal-budget single agents.
key_idea: Measure collaboration gain net of added budget.
relevance_rationale: Methodology for fair MAS-vs-single cost comparisons.
found_via: web search: science of scaling agents

title: Dr. MAS: Stable Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Agent LLM Systems
cost_reduction_reported: Heterogeneous agent-model assignment reported (in search summary) to cut latency 31.6% and API cost 41.8%; abstract states it remains effective under heterogeneous assignments while improving efficiency
summary: Dr. MAS diagnoses GRPO instability in multi-agent RL as a global normalization mismatch and fixes it with per-agent advantage normalization, plus a training framework with per-agent model serving. It supports heterogeneous agent-model assignments, e.g., smaller models for low-level agents.
key_idea: Per-agent advantage normalization for stable MAS RL, supporting heterogeneous models.
relevance_rationale: Training infrastructure for heterogeneous role models.

title: AgentConductor: Topology Evolution for Multi-Agent Competition-Level Code Generation
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 14.6% higher pass@1, 13% density reduction and 68% token-cost reduction vs strongest baseline
benchmarks: three competition-level and two foundational code datasets
summary: AgentConductor trains an LLM orchestrator with RL to infer roles and difficulty per query and build a density-controlled layered DAG topology, refining it with execution feedback. It improves competition-level code generation while cutting token cost.
key_idea: Difficulty-aware topology density control by an RL orchestrator.
relevance_rationale: Adaptive MAS structure for cost.

title: Budget-Aware Agentic Routing via Boundary-Guided Training
cost_reduction_reported: Matches strong routing baselines at substantially lower cost (no single number in abstract)
summary: Microsoft researchers cast agentic routing as a sequential, path-dependent decision between a cheap and an expensive model at each step under per-task budgets. Boundary-Guided Training uses always-small and always-large policies to build a difficulty taxonomy, then SFT and a policy-optimization method (BoPO) learn a router that improves the cost-success frontier.
key_idea: Learn per-step small/large routing anchored on boundary policies under budgets.
relevance_rationale: Directly addresses step-level routing in long-horizon agents.

title: SWE-Prot\'eg\'e: Learning to Selectively Collaborate With an Expert Unlocks Small Language Models as Software Engineering Agents
cost_reduction_reported: 42.4% Pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified with expert assistance ~4 calls per task and 11% of total tokens
summary: SWE-Protege post-trains a 7B coding model to remain the decision-maker while learning when to ask a strong expert model for help and how to follow its advice, using SFT on expert-augmented trajectories and RL that penalizes looping and unhelpful consultations. It reaches 42.4% on SWE-bench Verified with sparse expert use.
key_idea: Train the small agent to decide when to consult a large expert.
relevance_rationale: Learned step-level escalation in long-horizon coding agents.
found_via: arXiv title search: small language models agentic

title: CARD: Towards Conditional Design of Multi-agent Topological Structures
summary: CARD generates multi-agent communication topologies conditioned on environmental signals such as model upgrades, tool changes or resource availability, using a conditional variational graph encoder. Topologies adapt at training and run time and stay robust when model capabilities shift.
key_idea: Condition MAS topology generation on the current model/resource environment.
relevance_rationale: Topology adaptation to changing model pools.

title: Spend Less, Reason Better: Budget-Aware Value Tree Search for LLM Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Under strict low budgets, surpasses baseline performance obtained at 4x the resource allocation
summary: BAVT models multi-hop agent reasoning as a search tree guided by step-level residual value estimates, with a budget-conditioned node-selection rule that shifts from exploration to exploitation as budget depletes. It prunes redundant tool calls and beats parallel sampling at a quarter of the budget.
key_idea: Budget-conditioned tree search pruning low-value agent steps.
relevance_rationale: Per-step compute allocation within agents.

title: Adaptive Vision-Language Model Routing for Computer Use Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Projected inference cost reductions up to 78% while staying within 2 points of an all-large-model baseline
summary: Adaptive VLM Routing inserts a routing layer between a computer-use agent orchestrator and a pool of VLMs: for each tool call it estimates difficulty, probes a small VLM's confidence and sends the action to the cheapest model meeting a reliability threshold, escalating risky actions. Part of the vLLM Semantic Router project.
key_idea: Per-action VLM routing with confidence probing in computer-use agents.
relevance_rationale: Per-step model routing in GUI agents.

title: Efficient and Interpretable Multi-Agent LLM Routing via Ant Colony Optimization
cost_reduction_reported: Improves quality-cost trade-off over strong routing baselines (no single number in abstract)
summary: AMRO-S treats MAS routing as semantic-conditioned path selection, using a fine-tuned small LM for intent, task-specific ant-colony pheromone memories, and quality-gated asynchronous updates that learn without adding latency. It improves the quality-cost trade-off with interpretable routing traces.
key_idea: Ant-colony path selection over agents with asynchronous learning.
relevance_rationale: Online-updated MAS routing.

title: HyEvo: Self-Evolving Hybrid Agentic Workflows for Efficient Reasoning
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 19x lower inference cost and 16x lower latency vs state-of-the-art open-source baseline
summary: HyEvo evolves agentic workflows that mix LLM nodes with deterministic code nodes, offloading predictable operations from LLM inference, using a multi-island evolutionary search with reflection. It outperforms prior workflow generators while cutting cost and latency sharply.
key_idea: Replace predictable LLM steps with code nodes during workflow search.
relevance_rationale: Architecture-level cost lever: fewer LLM calls.

title: Utility-Guided Agent Orchestration for Efficient LLM Tool Use
summary: Formulates tool-using agent orchestration as an explicit decision among respond, retrieve, call tool, verify and stop, scored by estimated gain, step cost, uncertainty and redundancy. Compares against direct answering, fixed workflows and ReAct to study quality-cost trade-offs.
key_idea: Explicit utility-based policy over agent actions including stopping.
relevance_rationale: Controllable per-step cost policy.

title: Benchmarking Multi-Agent LLM Architectures for Financial Document Processing: A Comparative Study of Orchestration Patterns, Cost-Accuracy Tradeoffs and Production Scaling Strategies
cost_reduction_reported: Reflexive loop F1 0.943 at 2.3x sequential cost; hierarchical supervisor-worker F1 0.921 at 1.4x cost; hybrid configs recover 89% of reflexive gains at 1.15x cost
summary: Benchmarks four orchestration architectures (sequential, parallel fan-out, hierarchical supervisor-worker, reflexive loop) for financial document extraction across five LLMs, measuring F1, latency, cost per document and tokens. Hierarchical designs sit best on the cost-accuracy frontier, and hybrids with caching, model routing and adaptive retry get most of the accuracy at little extra cost.
key_idea: Orchestration pattern choice drives cost-accuracy; hybrids with routing recover most gains cheaply.
relevance_rationale: Production-style cost comparison of MAS patterns, including model routing ablations.

title: Efficient Benchmarking of AI Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Reduces number of evaluation tasks by 44-70% while keeping high rank fidelity
summary: Shows that small task subsets preserve agent rankings even under scaffold-driven distribution shift, and proposes evaluating new agents only on tasks with 30-70% historical pass rates. This cuts evaluation cost by 44-70% with reliable rankings.
key_idea: Evaluate on mid-difficulty tasks to rank agents cheaply.
relevance_rationale: Evaluation cost reduction; useful for config search budgets.

title: AgentCollab: A Self-Evaluation-Driven Collaboration Paradigm for Efficient LLM Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Consistently improves the accuracy-efficiency Pareto frontier (no single number in abstract)
summary: AgentCollab runs a cheap model by default and escalates control to a stronger model only when the agent's own self-reflection indicates it is not making progress, with a difficulty-aware cumulative escalation that allocates more budget after recent failures. The search summary notes that putting the large model on execution rather than planning gave higher accuracy.
key_idea: Self-evaluated progress triggers escalation to a stronger model mid-trajectory.
relevance_rationale: Step-level escalation without an external router.

title: Terminal Agents Suffice for Enterprise Automation
cost_reduction_reported: Terminal agents match or outperform more complex agent architectures at a fraction of the cost
summary: ServiceNow researchers argue a coding agent with only a terminal and filesystem, calling platform APIs directly, solves many enterprise automation tasks better and far more cheaply than MCP tool agents or GUI web agents. Suggests simple programmatic interfaces plus strong models as the enterprise backbone.
key_idea: A plain terminal coding agent beats heavier enterprise agent stacks on cost.
relevance_rationale: Direct enterprise evidence on architecture-level cost reduction.

title: Single-Agent LLMs Outperform Multi-Agent Systems on Multi-Hop Reasoning Under Equal Thinking Token Budgets
summary: Argues from the data processing inequality that under a fixed reasoning-token budget a single agent is more information-efficient than a multi-agent system, and confirms that single agents match or beat MAS on multi-hop reasoning at matched budgets. Flags API budget-control and benchmark artifacts that inflate reported MAS gains.
key_idea: At equal thinking-token budgets, single agents match or beat MAS.
relevance_rationale: Key controlled evidence on when MAS is worth it.

title: Explainable Model Routing for Agentic Workflows
summary: Topaz makes subtask-to-model routing in agentic workflows auditable, using skill-based capability profiles, traceable budget-based and multi-objective routing, and natural-language explanations so developers can tune cost-quality trade-offs.
key_idea: Interpretable, auditable subtask-level model routing.
relevance_rationale: Governance for step-level routing decisions.

title: Not All Turns Are Equally Hard: Adaptive Thinking Budgets For Efficient Multi-Turn Reasoning in Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 35% token savings and up to 30% latency reduction at maintained accuracy; TAB All-SubQ up to 40% savings
summary: Casts multi-turn agent reasoning as sequential compute allocation and trains a GRPO policy that assigns per-turn thinking budgets under a per-problem token limit, spending less on easy turns. It saves up to 35% of tokens without losing accuracy.
key_idea: Learned per-turn thinking budgets for agents.
relevance_rationale: Per-step compute allocation analogous to per-step downscaling.

title: AgentOpt v0.1 Technical Report: Client-Side Optimization for LLM-Based Agent
cost_reduction_reported: At matched accuracy, best vs worst model combinations differ 13-32x in cost; UCB-E recovers near-optimal accuracy with 62-76% less evaluation budget than brute force
summary: AgentOpt is a framework-agnostic client-side package that searches for the most cost-effective assignment of models to pipeline roles from a small evaluation set, using bandit and BO search algorithms. It shows huge cost spreads across model combinations and finds near-optimal assignments cheaply.
key_idea: Bandit search over per-role model assignments for agent pipelines.
relevance_rationale: Directly optimizes role-level model assignment with measured cost spreads.

title: Select-then-Solve: Paradigm Routing as Inference-Time Optimization for LLM Agents
summary: Compares six reasoning paradigms (Direct, CoT, ReAct, Plan-Execute, Reflection, ReCode) over four LLMs and ten benchmarks (~18,000 runs) and finds no paradigm dominates. A light embedding router that picks the paradigm per task raises average accuracy from 47.6% to 53.1%.
key_idea: Route each task to the best agent paradigm, not just the best model.
relevance_rationale: Architecture/paradigm routing per query.

title: ReDAct: Uncertainty-Aware Deferral for LLM Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Deferring about 15% of decisions to the large model matches exclusive large-model quality at significantly lower cost; search summary reports 64% savings vs GPT-5.2 alone
summary: ReDAct gives a ReAct-style agent a small default model and a large model, deferring an action to the large model when the small model's uncertainty exceeds a calibrated threshold. Deferring only about 15% of decisions matches large-model quality in embodied text environments.
key_idea: Uncertainty-triggered per-action deferral from small to large model.
relevance_rationale: Canonical step-level deferral inside agent loops.

title: Don't Overthink It: Inter-Rollout Action Agreement as a Free Adaptive-Compute Signal for LLM Agents
cost_reduction_reported: TrACE-4 matches SC-4 with 33-39% fewer LLM calls; TrACE-8 matches SC-8 with 55-65% fewer calls
summary: TrACE samples a few candidate next actions per step and commits immediately when they agree, sampling more only when agreement is low. It matches fixed self-consistency with far fewer calls, and agreement proves a reliable signal of step difficulty.
key_idea: Action agreement across rollouts as a free per-step difficulty signal.
relevance_rationale: Training-free step-level difficulty signal usable for escalation.

title: Pioneer Agent: Continual Improvement of Small Language Models in Production
summary: Pioneer Agent automates the lifecycle of specializing small models for production: data acquisition, evaluation set construction, training, and in production mode diagnosing labeled failures and retraining under regression constraints. It raises intent classification from 84.9% to 99.3% in a production-style deployment.
key_idea: Agent that continually specializes SLMs from production failures.
relevance_rationale: Supports replacing frontier calls with continually improved SLMs.

title: Small Model as Master Orchestrator: Learning Unified Agent-Tool Orchestration with Parallel Subtask Decomposition
summary: Agent-as-Tool unifies agents and tools into one learnable action space, and a lightweight orchestrator (ParaManager) trained with SFT and RL decomposes tasks into parallel subtasks and delegates them. It generalizes to unseen model pools.
key_idea: A small trained orchestrator delegates parallel subtasks to agents and tools.
relevance_rationale: Small-model orchestration of larger workers.

title: Phase-Scheduled Multi-Agent Systems for Token-Efficient Coordination
cost_reduction_reported: Mean 27.3% token reduction (21.4-34.8%) within 2.1 points of fully activated baseline
summary: PSMAS activates agents on a schedule derived from task dependencies so only agents within an active window run each step, while idle agents get compressed summaries. On LangGraph it cuts tokens by about 27% at near-baseline performance.
key_idea: Temporal scheduling of agent activation with compressed context for idle agents.
