title: Subagents vs Agent Skills: Executing Reusable Knowledge for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks
summary: Compares loading skill instructions into the main context against invoking skill packages as subagents with fresh context windows. Subagents win when skills have clear input-output contracts, at the price of extra coordination tokens.
key_idea: When to run reusable knowledge as subagents vs in-context skills.
relevance_rationale: Architecture trade-off relevant to subagent design.

title: OrchSLM: Probing the Dynamics of Small Language Model Orchestration
summary: OrchSLM studies non-interactive orchestration of heterogeneous small models, where each SLM generates candidates independently and a router selects among cached samples, exposing design choices like pool composition and consensus as controllable knobs.
key_idea: Probe of how routing over cached SLM outputs behaves.
relevance_rationale: SLM orchestration design space.
found_via: arXiv search: heterogeneous LLM multi-agent cost

title: RideWay: Benchmarking Efficient Task Completion for Tool-Using Language Agents
signals_used: Efficiency Utility (excess tool calls and turns)
summary: RideWay benchmarks tool-using ride-hailing agents on efficiency, discounting successes for excess tool calls and user turns relative to reference effort, calibrated with human preferences. Excess turns are penalized about twice as much as excess tool calls.
key_idea: Success-gated efficiency metric for tool-using agents.
relevance_rationale: Efficiency-aware agent evaluation.
found_via: arXiv title search: tool-use efficiency agent

title: AgentRouter: Heterogeneous Model Routing for Cost-Optimal Multi-Step Agentic Workflows
cost_reduction_reported: 72% cost reduction vs frontier-only while retaining 97.3% of frontier quality; RouteLLM and FrugalGPT applied per-step achieve 31% and 44%
benchmarks: planning, coding, research and data-analysis agent trajectories (50,000 annotated steps)
summary: AgentRouter is a 12M-parameter classifier (<5ms per step) that maps each trajectory step to one of four model tiers from five features, trained on 50,000 annotated steps. It cuts cost 72% versus frontier-only with under 3% quality loss and beats per-step RouteLLM and FrugalGPT.
key_idea: Lightweight per-step tier classifier for agent trajectories.
relevance_rationale: Direct step-level routing with strong reported savings.

title: Total Cost of Agency: Exact Attribution of Memory Injection Cost in Multi-Agent LLM Workflows
cost_reduction_reported: Memory injection is ~12% of full billed cost, rising to 27.6% at workflow depth six; shrinking retrieval window 32 to 2 cuts injected tokens 28.7%
benchmarks: 200-task enterprise benchmark on real model APIs
summary: Decomposes multi-agent workflow cost into base prompt, inference, memory injection, miss penalty and context accumulation, with an exact two-pass token attribution. On an enterprise benchmark, injected memory is a growing share of cost with workflow depth and is controllable.
key_idea: Attribute MAS bills to memory injection and control it.
relevance_rationale: Cost accounting for MAS in production-like settings.

title: Do We Need Complex Topology Control? Distinct-Peer Random Routing Improves Cost-Efficiency in Sparse Multi-Agent Debate
summary: Finds that a simple random-without-replacement peer routing, where each agent debates two new distinct peers per round, is a strong baseline that improves the accuracy-cost trade-off of sparse debate, and that light stopping rules cut cost further. Argues learned topology control must beat these simple baselines.
key_idea: Simple random sparse routing plus stopping rivals learned topologies.
relevance_rationale: Strong cheap baseline for MAS topology work.

title: Analyzing and Mitigating Cost-Inefficient Behaviors in Coding Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Three inefficient behaviors affect 79-98% of tasks and up to 22.75% of cost; developer-designed skills cut cost by up to 41.73%
summary: Analyzes 1,200 coding-agent trajectories (Claude Code, Mini-SWE-Agent) and identifies three recurring wasteful behaviors: subsumed retrieval, similar script generation and test re-execution. Developer-written skills reduce cost up to 42%, while structure-aware retrieval and agent-synthesized skills help less or even raise cost.
key_idea: Target recurring wasteful behaviors in coding agents with human-designed skills.
relevance_rationale: Token-consumption analysis with mitigation for coding agents.
found_via: web search: AI agents that matter

title: Learning What to Skip: Counterfactual Credit Assignment for Efficient Multi-Agent LLM Workflows
cost_reduction_reported: Reduces recorded token cost while matching or improving full-workflow accuracy (no single number in abstract)
summary: LW2S learns from controlled skip interventions on full-workflow logs which planning, verification or summarization components can be safely omitted given the current state, with held-out calibration and guards. It lowers token cost at equal accuracy.
key_idea: Counterfactual credit assignment to skip unneeded workflow components.
relevance_rationale: Learning component-level omission from logs.
found_via: arXiv search: cost-efficient LLM agent model selection

title: HM-ROUTER: Joint Model and Harness Routing for Agentic Systems
cost_reduction_reported: Leads at all seven evaluated cost budgets; +7.3 points mean routing accuracy over strongest learned baseline
benchmarks: benchmark from 12 public agent benchmarks (293 routes, 73 models, 25 harnesses)
summary: HM-Router jointly selects a model and an agent harness per query, learning shared model and harness representations with a tensor-decomposition interaction term so it can predict unobserved model-harness pairs. It beats learned baselines across cost budgets.
key_idea: Route over (model, harness) pairs, not just models.
relevance_rationale: Configuration-level routing for agents.

title: Planner-as-Router: Joint Plan-Time Model Routing for Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent Workflows
cost_reduction_reported: Cuts cost 44% vs all-frontier routing while giving up 2.9 accuracy points; matches frontier-on-sink heuristic and beats FrugalGPT cascade on cost
benchmarks: EntBench (54 enterprise tasks with live SQL/MongoDB grading)
summary: Planner-as-Router has the planner assign a model tier (small, mid, frontier) to each subtask as it decomposes the query, so the whole workflow's dependencies inform tier choice without a separate router or training data. On an enterprise benchmark graded against live databases it stays on the cost-accuracy frontier.
key_idea: Let the planner pick each subtask's model tier at plan time.
relevance_rationale: Training-free subtask-level model assignment in enterprise workflows.

title: RSI-Router: Evolving Subtask-Level LLM Routing and Skills for Cost-Efficient Agents
cost_reduction_reported: Surpasses DeepSeek-only baseline at about 48.3% of the cost across five agentic benchmarks; 74.7-82.2% cost cuts with better performance on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop; +16.7% relative on Terminal-Bench 2.0 at 18.0% lower cost
summary: RSI-Router mines subtask definitions from trajectories, evolves subtask-to-model assignments, develops model-specific skills by comparing routed and large-only runs, and keeps a Pareto population of routers across iterations. Routing between a large and a 9B model halves cost while improving performance.
key_idea: Recursive self-improvement of subtask-level routing and skills.
relevance_rationale: Subtask-level large-small collaboration with strong savings.

title: Building effective agents
summary: Anthropic distills lessons from dozens of customer agent deployments: prefer simple composable workflow patterns (prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer) and only move to autonomous agents when needed, since agentic systems trade latency and cost for performance. The routing pattern explicitly sends easy questions to smaller models such as Haiku and hard ones to Sonnet.
key_idea: Start simple; add agentic complexity only when it pays for its cost; route easy inputs to smaller models.
relevance_rationale: Seed; widely used practitioner guidance on architecture-level cost decisions, based on customer deployments.

title: How we built our multi-agent research system
cost_reduction_reported: Not a cost reduction: Opus 4 lead + Sonnet 4 subagents outperformed single-agent Opus 4 by 90.2% on an internal research eval; agents use ~4x chat tokens and multi-agent systems ~15x; token usage explained 80% of BrowseComp performance variance; parallel tool calls cut research time up to 90%
summary: Describes the production Claude Research system, where an Opus lead agent plans and spawns parallel Sonnet subagents with their own context windows. The heterogeneous setup beat single-agent Opus by 90.2% on an internal eval but used about 15x the tokens of chat, so it pays off only for high-value, parallelizable, context-heavy tasks.
key_idea: Big-model lead with smaller-model parallel subagents buys quality with tokens; worth it only for high-value breadth tasks.
relevance_rationale: Seed; production evidence of role-level model assignment and multi-agent token overhead.

title: Building multi-agent systems: When and how to use them
cost_reduction_reported: States multi-agent systems typically use 3-10x more tokens than single-agent approaches for equivalent tasks
summary: Anthropic guidance recommending single agents by default and multi-agent designs only for context protection, parallelization or specialization, since coordination costs otherwise exceed benefits. Reports that multi-agent systems usually spend 3-10x more tokens due to duplicated context, coordination messages and summarization, and advises decomposing by context boundaries.
key_idea: Use multi-agent only for context isolation, parallelism or specialization; otherwise it costs 3-10x more tokens.
relevance_rationale: Practitioner guidance grounded in customer deployments on when MAS is worth its cost.
found_via: web search: Anthropic multi-agent research system

title: The advisor strategy: Give Sonnet an intelligence boost with Opus
cost_reduction_reported: Sonnet executor + Opus advisor: +2.7 points on SWE-bench Multilingual over Sonnet alone with 11.9% lower cost per agentic task; Haiku + Opus advisor: 41.2% vs 19.7% on BrowseComp, trailing Sonnet solo by 29% but 85% cheaper per task
summary: Anthropic's advisor tool lets a cheaper executor model run an agentic task end to end and consult a stronger advisor model mid-task for a plan or correction, all inside one API request, with advisor tokens billed at advisor rates. Vendor benchmarks show quality gains with lower or similar cost, especially for weaker executors.
key_idea: Cheap executor runs the loop and calls an expensive advisor only at hard decision points.
relevance_rationale: Productized step-level escalation pattern with vendor-reported cost and quality numbers.

title: Optimizing for cost and intelligence
cost_reduction_reported: Examples reported: prompt caching cut DeepResearch Bench II cost 81% (Fable 5.1) and 62.5% (Sonnet 5); on SWE-bench Pro, Opus 5.5 low effort with failures re-run at high reached 97% at ~$0.17/task vs 95.3% at $0.29 all-high; Fable 5 coordinator + Sonnet 5 worker cost ~50% of solo Fable 5 on an easy BrowseComp slice; on full BrowseComp, solo Fable 5 at lower effort was 22-30% cheaper than the orchestrator at same accuracy
summary: Anthropic documentation with measured results on cost levers: caching, trimming tools and context, effort tuning, retrying failures at higher effort, task budgets, advisor pairing and orchestrator-worker delegation. It reports that advisor gains shrink as the executor approaches the advisor's capability and that cheaper-worker delegation helps on easy slices but can lose to a solo model at lower effort on the full set.
key_idea: Vendor-measured playbook of per-step and architecture cost levers, including when delegation to cheaper workers loses.
relevance_rationale: Rare quantitative vendor evidence comparing escalation, effort control and orchestrator-worker model splits on agentic benchmarks.

title: A practical guide to building agents
summary: OpenAI's guide, distilled from customer deployments, recommends maximizing a single agent before splitting into manager or decentralized multi-agent patterns. On model selection it advises prototyping with the most capable model for every task to set a baseline, then swapping in smaller models where they remain acceptable, since simple retrieval or intent classification steps may not need the smartest model.
key_idea: Baseline with the strongest model everywhere, then downscale per task; prefer a single agent until complexity demands more.
relevance_rationale: Seed; canonical practitioner recipe for per-step model downscaling and architecture choice.

title: How and when to build multi-agent systems
summary: Harrison Chase reconciles Anthropic's multi-agent research post with Cognition's 'don't build multi-agents' argument: multi-agent systems suit read-heavy, breadth-first, parallelizable tasks whose value justifies high token spend, while write-heavy tasks with shared context and many interdependencies are poor fits. Context engineering is framed as the main job.
key_idea: Multi-agent fits parallel read-heavy tasks worth the token cost; avoid it for tightly coupled writes.
relevance_rationale: Practitioner synthesis on when MAS is worth it.
found_via: web search: Anthropic multi-agent research system

title: MAS-Orchestra: Understanding and Improving Multi-Agent Reasoning Through Holistic Orchestration and Controlled Benchmarks
signals_used: task structure axes (depth, horizon, breadth, parallel, robustness)
cost_reduction_reported: More than 10x efficiency over strong baselines while improving accuracy
summary: MAS-Orchestra trains an orchestrator with function-calling RL to generate an entire MAS at once, treating sub-agents as callable functions. Its controlled MASBENCH shows MAS gains depend on task depth, horizon, breadth, parallelism and robustness and on orchestrator and sub-agent capability, not universally.
key_idea: Holistic RL orchestration plus a benchmark of when MAS beats single agents.
relevance_rationale: Both a cost-efficient orchestrator and evidence on when MAS helps.

title: COLLATOR: Compositional Multi-Agent Orchestration with Counterfactual Reinforcement Learning
cost_reduction_reported: Best average performance among evaluated orchestration methods with improved accuracy-token trade-off
summary: LEMON is an LLM orchestrator that writes a unified orchestration spec of agent duties, capacity levels and dependencies per task, trained with GRPO plus localized counterfactual credit that edits individual role, capacity or dependency fields. It improves accuracy per token.
key_idea: Learn capacity (model-size) assignment per agent with counterfactual credit.
relevance_rationale: Per-agent capacity assignment with fine-grained credit.

title: When Cloud Agents Meet Device Agents: Lessons from Hybrid Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Qualcomm researchers adapt two MAS architectures for hybrid on-device SLM and cloud LLM inference and map how design choices move systems along the Pareto frontier of power, cost and accuracy. SLMs benefit from LLM help, but the best hybrid architecture is task-dependent and more frontier compute does not reliably help.
key_idea: Systematic design-space study of hybrid SLM/LLM multi-agent systems.
relevance_rationale: Evidence on role-level placement of small vs large models.

title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Efficiency Methods for Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Argues that reported gains of MAS efficiency methods (agent pruning, edge removal, compact structure search) are often overestimated because of method-specific prompts, starting topologies and non-MAS-demanding tasks where random pruning already works. A controlled benchmark shows many gains come from structural collapse or disabled tools.
key_idea: Many MAS pruning gains vanish under controlled, MAS-demanding evaluation.
relevance_rationale: Critical check on the AgentPrune/AgentDropout line of work.

title: When Do Multi-Agent Systems Help? An Information Bottleneck Perspective
summary: Frames the MAS vs single-agent difference as an information bottleneck: a single agent keeps its full trace in one context while a MAS relays bounded messages between isolated contexts. MAS advantages arise only under bounded relays, where compression trades efficiency against loss of task-relevant information.
key_idea: MAS helps only when bounded-message compression is beneficial.
relevance_rationale: Theory for when MAS is worth it.

title: On Time, Within Budget: Constraint-Driven Online Resource Allocation for Agentic Workflows
cost_reduction_reported: Consistently improves constrained completion probability over strong baselines
summary: Studies allocating models and parallel samples to subtasks of a dependency-structured agent workflow so it finishes within a budget and deadline, via Monte Carlo Portfolio Planning that simulates executions and replans after outcomes.
key_idea: Online subtask-to-model allocation maximizing on-time, in-budget completion.
relevance_rationale: Per-subtask model assignment under hard budgets.

title: Learning Latency-Aware Orchestration for Multi-Agent Systems
cost_reduction_reported: Over 50% end-to-end latency reduction at competitive or better accuracy
summary: LAMaS learns latency-aware MAS execution graphs with critical-path-aware credit assignment and adds a runtime controller that eliminates redundant future agent interactions. It halves latency without losing accuracy.
key_idea: Optimize the critical path, not just total cost, in MAS.
relevance_rationale: Latency counterpart to MAS cost optimization.

title: SLMs as Multi-Agent Routers: A Progressive SFT and Reinforcement Learning Approach
summary: Trains a small language model with SFT then RL to select which specialized retrieval agent to call and to generate its tool parameters, rewarding retrieval relevance rather than inferred intent. The SLM router learns which agents reliably return relevant results.
key_idea: A small RL-trained model routes among retrieval agents.
relevance_rationale: SLM-based routing among agents.

title: AgentFloor: How Far Up the tool use Ladder Can Small Open-Weight Models Go?
cost_reduction_reported: Strongest open-weight model matches GPT-5 on the benchmark while being substantially cheaper and faster
summary: AgentFloor is a 30-task ladder from instruction following to long-horizon planning, run with 16 open models and GPT-5 over 16,542 scored runs. Small and mid-size open models handle most short, structured tool-use steps, while frontier models keep an edge on long-horizon planning.
key_idea: Map which agent step types need frontier models.
relevance_rationale: Empirical basis for per-step downscaling decisions.

title: ToolOrchestra: Elevating Intelligence via Efficient Model and Tool Orchestration
cost_reduction_reported: HLE 37.1% vs GPT-5 35.1% while 2.5x more efficient; on tau2-Bench and FRAMES beats GPT-5 at about 30% of the cost
summary: NVIDIA's ToolOrchestra trains a small 8B orchestrator with RL to coordinate tools and other models, including larger LLMs, with rewards for outcome, efficiency and user tool preferences. The Orchestrator beats GPT-5 on HLE at 2.5x better efficiency and on tau2-Bench and FRAMES at about 30% of the cost.
key_idea: A small RL-trained orchestrator decides when to call expensive models and tools.
relevance_rationale: Strong evidence that a small model can route per step among models and tools cost-effectively.

title: Slm-mux: Orchestrating small language models for reasoning
cost_reduction_reported: With two SLMs, outperforms Qwen 2.5 72B on GPQA and GSM8K and matches it on MATH; up to +13.4% on MATH vs prior orchestration
summary: SLM-MUX orchestrates multiple small models, with a search for the most complementary subset and SLM-specific test-time scaling, showing that orchestration methods designed for frontier models underperform with SLMs. Two SLMs can beat a 72B model on some reasoning benchmarks.
key_idea: Orchestrate complementary SLMs instead of calling a large model.
relevance_rationale: SLM ensembles as a substitute for large-model calls.

title: Planner-R1: Reward Shaping Enables Efficient Agentic RL with Smaller LLMs
cost_reduction_reported: 8B models 3.5x more compute-efficient and 1.5x more memory-efficient than 32B with competitive performance; 56.9% final pass vs GPT-5 21.2% on TravelPlanner
summary: Agentic RL on TravelPlanner with reward shaping reaches 56.9% final pass with 180 training queries; shaped dense rewards let 8B models match 32B at much lower compute.
key_idea: Reward shaping makes small models efficient agentic planners.
relevance_rationale: Background on training small agent models.

title: ProST: Progressive Sub-task Training for Pareto-Optimal Multi-agent Systems Using Small Language Models
cost_reduction_reported: Progressive sub-task training improves effectiveness of SLM multi-agent systems at all configurations (Pareto analysis in paper)
summary: Compares single-agent LLM systems with multi-agent SLM systems on AppWorld for effectiveness and efficiency, finding SLMs struggle with long trajectories even with role specialization. Progressive sub-task training, a curriculum over subtasks, improves SLM multi-agent results.
key_idea: Curriculum over subtasks to make SLM role agents Pareto-competitive.
relevance_rationale: Single-LLM vs multi-SLM trade-off with training fix.

title: The Cost of Dynamic Reasoning: Demystifying AI Agents and Test-Time Scaling from an AI Infrastructure Perspective
cost_reduction_reported: Agents show rapidly diminishing accuracy returns with increased compute (system-level resource, latency, energy and power analysis)
summary: A system-level analysis of AI agents quantifying resource use, latency, energy and datacenter power across agent designs and test-time scaling strategies. Accuracy gains from more compute diminish quickly while infrastructure costs grow, raising sustainability concerns.
key_idea: Agents' compute returns diminish fast; system costs do not.
relevance_rationale: Infrastructure view on agent cost.

title: Joint Continual Learning of Local Language Models and Cloud Offloading Decisions with Budget Constraints
summary: DA-GRPO lets a local SLM jointly learn task skill and when to request cloud LLM help during continual learning, building a cloud-usage budget directly into GRPO advantages. It reduces forgetting and keeps cloud usage stable.
key_idea: Budget-constrained RL teaches a local model when to offload to the cloud.
relevance_rationale: Learned escalation policy under a budget.

title: An Exact Generate - Transform Decomposition of Small-LLM Team Scaling Across Orchestration Architectures
cost_reduction_reported: At equal call budgets token cost still varies 2.1x across architectures
summary: Sweeps eight orchestration architectures with 7-9B models up to 30 calls and finds team-scaling returns are sharply task-dependent: large on arithmetic, small on multiple-choice. An exact generate-transform decomposition explains which architectures convert extra candidates into accuracy.
key_idea: Team scaling is a task- and architecture-specific bet.
relevance_rationale: Evidence on the value of adding agents.

title: Cost-Utility Alignment in LLM Agent Trajectories:Profiling,Attribution,Diagnosis,Adaptation,and Evaluation
summary: A framework and survey for judging whether an agent trajectory's resource spend is justified by its task contribution, organized into cost profiling, utility attribution, misalignment diagnosis, targeted adaptation and evaluation.
key_idea: Treat cost and utility as dual ledgers over agent trajectories.
relevance_rationale: Framework for per-step cost-value analysis.

title: When Does LLM Orchestration Pay Off? A Controlled Evaluation of Accuracy, Cost, and Task Difficulty
cost_reduction_reported: Largest gain 4.6 points over optimized CoT while needing roughly 2-4x the tokens of task-only inference
summary: A controlled comparison of Self-Refine, Best-of-N and Debate against optimized single-call baselines, with equal GEPA optimization budgets. Orchestration gives modest benchmark-dependent gains at 2-4x tokens, does not help more on harder items, and depends strongly on the backbone.
key_idea: Orchestration gains are modest, model-specific and costly.
relevance_rationale: Controlled evidence on when multi-call orchestration is worth it.

title: CASTER: Breaking the Cost-Performance Barrier in Multi-Agent Orchestration via Context-Aware Strategy for Task Efficient Routing
cost_reduction_reported: Up to 72.4% lower inference cost than strong-model baselines at matched success rates
summary: CASTER is a lightweight router for graph-based MAS that estimates each node's task difficulty from semantic and structural features and picks a model, self-improving from its own routing failures. It cuts cost substantially versus using strong models everywhere.
key_idea: Per-node difficulty router for graph MAS, trained from its own failures.
relevance_rationale: Node-level model routing in MAS.

title: FutureWeaver: Planning Test-Time Compute for Multi-Agent Systems with Modularized Collaboration
summary: FutureWeaver plans test-time compute allocation across a multi-agent system under a fixed budget, using collaboration modules induced by self-play reflection and dual-level planning over short-horizon actions and long-horizon abstractions.
key_idea: Budgeted planning of compute across MAS collaboration modules.
relevance_rationale: Budget allocation within MAS.

title: Inefficiencies of Meta Agents for Agent Design
cost_reduction_reported: Automated design plus deployment is cheaper than human-designed agents in only two datasets when deployed on over 15,000 examples
summary: Examines meta-agents that design agents: expanding context with all prior designs underperforms, designed agents lack diversity, and the design cost is recouped only in a few datasets at large deployment scale.
key_idea: Automated agent design rarely pays back its design cost.
relevance_rationale: Cost accounting for automated MAS design.

title: SeqRoute: Global Budget-Aware Sequential LLM Routing via Offline Reinforcement Learning
cost_reduction_reported: 6.0-73.5% lower operational cost at maintained or improved quality with bankruptcy rates under 1%
summary: SeqRoute treats routing over a multi-turn session with a global budget as a finite-horizon MDP solved with conservative Q-learning, augmenting 10,000 logged sessions into 2.38M transitions via hindsight budget relabeling. It avoids spending the budget early and navigates the Pareto frontier without retraining.
key_idea: Offline RL for budget-aware routing over sequential turns.
relevance_rationale: Sequential routing learned from logs; transferable to steps.

title: Inference Economics of Enterprise Coding Agents: A Case Study of Cloud vs. On-Premise LLMs
cost_reduction_reported: Prompt caching (99.3% hit rate) cut realized API cost 88.6% to $0.57 per million tokens; on-prem saves 40.1% TCO under shared GPUs but dedicated reservation costs 43.8% more; local config had fix-commit ratio 74.9% vs 45.9%
summary: A longitudinal single-developer case study on a production monorepo comparing API Claude Opus in Claude Code against on-prem quantized GLM in Opencode. Caching makes the API cheaper per token than on-prem, the local model causes far more repair commits, and hybrid routing gateways trade defect rate for savings rather than dominating.
key_idea: Real telemetry: caching reshapes cloud vs on-prem agent economics.
relevance_rationale: Production evidence on coding-agent cost levers and routing trade-offs.

title: In-Context Prompting Obsoletes Agent Orchestration for Procedural Tasks
cost_reduction_reported: In-context approach scores 4.53-5.00 vs 4.17-4.84 for LangGraph orchestration; failure rates 11.5%/0.5%/5% vs 24%/9%/17%
summary: For procedural multi-turn tasks, putting the whole procedure in the system prompt and letting the model self-orchestrate beats an external LangGraph orchestrator on quality and failure rate across three domains. External orchestration is argued to be unnecessary for modern frontier models on such tasks.
key_idea: Self-orchestration in context beats external orchestrators for procedures.
relevance_rationale: Architecture simplification evidence.

title: Cost-of-Pass: An Economic Framework for Evaluating Language Models
signals_used: expected cost of a correct solution
summary: Defines cost-of-pass, the expected monetary cost of producing a correct solution, and the frontier cost-of-pass across models and human experts. Finds lightweight models most cost-effective for basic quantitative tasks, large models for knowledge-intensive ones and reasoning models for complex math.
key_idea: Cost-of-pass as an economic metric for model selection.
relevance_rationale: Metric used by Efficient Agents and useful for per-step model choice.

title: E$^3$-Orch: Towards Effective, Efficient, and Extensible Agentic Orchestration with Reinforcement Learning
summary: E3-Orch trains an orchestration policy with RL around a milestone-plan-act workflow: for each milestone it plans dependencies, assigns subtasks to suitable executors and runs independent ones in parallel.
key_idea: Milestone-scoped RL orchestration with executor assignment.
relevance_rationale: Learned executor assignment.

title: EvolveRouter: Co-Evolving Routing and Prompt for Multi-Agent Question Answering
summary: EvolveRouter co-evolves graph-based query routing among agents with targeted instruction refinement of the agents, and adapts the number of collaborating agents per query at inference.
key_idea: Co-evolve routing and agent prompts; adapt team size per query.
relevance_rationale: Routing among agents with adaptive team size.

title: EMS: Multi-Agent Voting via Efficient Majority-then-Stopping
summary: EMS calls agents in order of retrieved historical reliability for similar queries and stops voting once the leading answer cannot be overturned, avoiding redundant agent calls in majority voting.
key_idea: Reliability-ordered agent calls with early stopping of votes.
relevance_rationale: Cuts multi-agent voting cost.

title: Dynamic Mixed-Precision Routing for Efficient Multi-step LLM Interaction
cost_reduction_reported: Strong accuracy-cost trade-off over single-precision baselines
summary: DMR routes each decision step of a long-horizon agent between a high-precision and a low-precision quantized LLM, trained with KL-based supervision to find precision-sensitive steps and then GRPO. It improves the accuracy-cost trade-off.
key_idea: Per-step routing between full-precision and quantized models.
relevance_rationale: Step-level downscaling via quantization rather than model size.

title: Learning to Orchestrate Agents in Natural Language with the Conductor
summary: A 7B Conductor trained with RL learns coordination strategies over pools of powerful worker LLMs, designing communication topologies and writing focused instructions, and beats any individual worker on hard reasoning benchmarks. Trained on randomized pools, it adapts to arbitrary agent sets.
key_idea: Small RL-trained conductor orchestrates large worker LLMs.
relevance_rationale: Small-orchestrator/large-worker pattern.

title: Talk to Right Specialists: Iterative Routing in Multi-agent Systems for Question Answering
summary: RIRS routes questions only to the most relevant RAG agents using embedding summaries of their private corpora, and iteratively aggregates and refines for complex questions, avoiding broadcast-to-all costs.
key_idea: Route questions to relevant specialist agents instead of broadcasting.
relevance_rationale: Routing among agents to save calls.

title: Improving the Efficiency of Language Agent Teams with Adaptive Task Graphs
summary: LATTE lets an LLM team co-build and maintain a shared task graph of subtask dependencies, assignments and progress, reducing wasted time, tokens and file operations compared with unstructured teams.
key_idea: Shared evolving task graph to cut MAS coordination waste.
relevance_rationale: MAS efficiency via coordination structure.

title: HieraMAS: Optimizing Intra-Node LLM Mixtures and Inter-Node Topology for Multi-Agent Systems
summary: HieraMAS implements each MAS role as a supernode mixing several heterogeneous LLMs in a propose-synthesize structure and jointly optimizes intra-node mixtures and inter-node topology, addressing credit assignment when outcomes depend on backbone capability.
key_idea: Optimize LLM mixtures inside each role plus topology.
relevance_rationale: Role-level heterogeneous model assignment.

title: Agent-GSPO: Communication-Efficient Multi-Agent Systems via Group Sequence Policy Optimization
cost_reduction_reported: State-of-the-art on seven reasoning benchmarks with a fraction of existing methods' token consumption
summary: Agent-GSPO trains MAS agents with sequence-level RL on a communication-aware reward that penalizes verbosity, leading to emergent strategic silence and much lower token use.
key_idea: RL with verbosity penalties for token-economical MAS.
relevance_rationale: Training-based MAS cost reduction.

title: Heterogeneous Swarms: Jointly Optimizing Model Roles and Weights for Multi-LLM Systems
summary: Heterogeneous Swarms jointly optimizes which LLMs play which roles in a DAG and their weights using particle swarm optimization, outperforming 15 role- or weight-based baselines by 18.5% on average.
key_idea: Swarm search over model roles (DAG) and weights.
relevance_rationale: Role assignment among heterogeneous models; quality-focused.

title: AFlow: Automating Agentic Workflow Generation
cost_reduction_reported: Enables smaller models to outperform GPT-4o on specific tasks at 4.55% of its inference cost in dollars; +5.7% average over SOTA baselines
summary: AFlow searches code-represented agentic workflows with MCTS, refining them from execution feedback. Beyond a 5.7% average gain, optimized workflows let smaller models beat GPT-4o on some tasks at under 5% of its cost.
key_idea: Workflow search lets small models replace large ones.
relevance_rationale: Architecture search as a downscaling lever.

title: From Deferral to Learning: Online In-Context Knowledge Distillation for LLM Cascades
